description: The RFC 6749 §4.1 authorization-code grant (+ OIDC Core 1.0 id_token) as orderable dance cards. The oauth-oidc-sim runs the state machine: the canonical order reaches resource access; calling the resource server before the token exchange raises the real invalid_request (the valet key was never obtained); a missing code raises invalid_request; a bad grant raises invalid_grant.

provenance.reference: RFC 6749 §4.1 (authorization-code grant), §4.1.2.1 + §5.2 (error codes: invalid_request, invalid_grant, …), RFC 6750 §3.1 (Bearer / 401), OpenID Connect Core 1.0 §3.1 (authentication request / id_token)
provenance.example_values: the code 'SplxlOBeZQQYbYS6WxSbIA' and access_token '2YotnFZFEjr1zCsicMWpAA' are the literal example values from RFC 6749 §4.1.2 / §5.1
provenance.reproducible_against: a real IdP authorize/token endpoint produces this exact act ordering; an out-of-order resource call returns the OAuth error JSON {"error":"invalid_request"}
provenance.honesty_note: Authored from RFC 6749 / OIDC Core with citation (the act NAMES and error STRINGS are the spec's literal values); the state machine is the consequence engine — the error a wrong move raises is computed, not authored.
